title: Windowed segment reconciliation and degraded reconnect negotiation for SSE streams
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Add a negotiation and reconciliation layer for windowed SSE fragments to allow degraded reconnects where clients may accept partially overlapping or lossy windows without breaking function-call/structured-output boundaries. Goal: reduce client-visible errors during short outages and make reconnect behavior explicit and interoperable with existing JSONL/eventstream shims.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol: servers advertise a rolling window token (window_id + start_offset + end_offset) in SSE comment frames that can be used to negotiate a degraded reconnect.

Clients can request either strict replay (full contiguous resume) or degraded resume (server may send a merged delta of the last N tokens) and receive an explicit status code explaining the trade-off.
Function-call boundaries are preserved: server must mark partial function-call frames and either re-send whole call or annotate with "repaired":true so client SDKs can detect and re-run validation.
End-to-end interop test against existing eventstream -> SSE shim demonstrates successful resume in at least 3 outage patterns (short gap, overlapping duplicates, truncated tail).
Documentation and SDK changes: Node/Python SDKs expose new reconnect negotiation flags and helper utilities for merging fragmented JSONL objects.
technical_notes: We will reuse existing resume-token format but extend it with window metadata: token := base_resume_token | window:{id, start_seq, end_seq, checksum}.
Trade-offs: degraded resume reduces token retransmit cost and tail latency but can introduce duplicated semantic outputs; prefer idempotent-by-default responses or application-layer dedupe hooks.

Server-side: implement a reconciliation pass that can generate a minimal 'repair delta' instead of full historical replay. The delta will include provenance headers for each chunk to allow clients to rehydrate accurately.

Client-side: SDK will need to expose a validation callback for structured outputs to decide whether to accept a repaired tail or request strict replay. Default behaviour: accept repaired unless strictResume flag is set.
decisions: Default reconnect mode = degraded if client does not opt into strictResume (reduces average reconnect latency).
Mark partial function-call frames with 'partial_call':true and include 'call_id' and 'sequence' to allow correct reassembly or safe retry.
Use SSE comment frames (":") for lightweight window advertisements to maintain HTTP/1.1 SSE compatibility.
Checksum uses CRC32C on byte-level chunk sequence to keep metadata small; not a cryptographic signature.
tasks: Server: implement window token header emission and repair-delta generator (ENG-119123-1).
Server: add tests for overlap/duplicate handling and measurable latency regression (<5ms per reconnect).
SDK: Node + Python add reconnect negotiation flags and partial-call reassembly helpers (ENG-119123-2).
Docs: PRD + protocol spec in Confluence and example client-server traces (ENG-119123-3).
Integration: run interop test against eventstream shim and dedicated instances (ENG-119123-4).
